COUNTY OF El DORADO
             PLANNING AND BUILDING DEPARTMENT
                   PLANNING COMMISSION
                       STAFF REPORT
                                         Date:                         October 22, 2026

                                         Staff:                        Cameron Morris


         TENTATIVE SUBDIVISION MAP TIME EXTENSION
FILE NUMBER:               TM-E26-0001/Southpointe Meadows

APPLICANT/
OWNER:                     Bianchi Tillett Developers

ENGINEER:                  Jay Goni, CNA Engineering

REQUEST:                   Request for three (3) one-year discretionary time extensions to
                           approved Southpointe Meadows Tentative Subdivision Map
                           (TM16-1529) creating seven (7) residential lots ranging in size
                           from 1 to 1.3 acres resulting in a new expiration date of October
                           26, 2029.

LOCATION:                  On the east side of Castec Way, approximately 1,200 feet east of
                           the intersection with Lakehills Drive, in the El Dorado Hills area,
                           Supervisorial District 1. (Exhibits A, B)

APN:                       110-450-007 (Exhibit C)

ACREAGE:                   8.04 acres

GENERAL PLAN:              Medium Density Residential (MDR) (Exhibit D)

ZONING:                    One-acre Residential (R1A) (Exhibit E)

ENVIRONMENTAL DOCUMENT:                  Previously Adopted Mitigated Negative Declaration

RECOMMENDATION:            Staff recommending the Planning Commission take the following
                           actions:

1.     Find Tentative Subdivision Map Time Extension TM-E26-0001 consistent with the
       Mitigated Negative Declaration adopted for the approved tentative map pursuant to
       Section 15162 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines
       (Subsequent Environmental Impact Report [EIRs] and Negative Declarations); and




                                                                     26-1601 A Page 1 of 4

TM-E26-0001/Southpointe Meadows
                                                                Planning Commission/October 22, 2026
                                                                                        Staff Report
                                                                                              Page 2

2.     Approve Tentative Subdivision Map Time Extension TM-E26-0001 granting three (3)
       one-year discretionary time extensions to approved Tentative Map TM16-1529
       (Southpointe Meadows), resulting in a new expiration date of October 26, 2029, based on
       the Findings and subject to the original Conditions of Approval as presented.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The Southpointe Meadows Tentative Subdivision Map (TM16-1529) is an approved tentative
map consisting of seven (7) single-family residential lots ranging from 1 to 1.3 acres. All parcels
would be served with public water and sewer service from El Dorado Irrigation District (EID).
Access to the parcels would come from South Meadows Court, a proposed private road,
connecting to Villa Del Sol, an existing private road. Since approval of the Tentative Subdivision
Map on October 26, 2017, the applicant has made diligent progress toward satisfying project
Conditions of Approval for the purpose of creation and development of these lots. The applicant
is requesting additional time to complete all requirements before recordation of the Final Map
and anticipates required work would be completed prior to expiration.

BACKGROUND

The Southpointe Meadows Tentative Subdivision Map (TM16-1529) was originally approved by
the Planning Commission on October 26, 2017 (Legistar File 17-1143) (Exhibit F). This
approval would create seven (7) residential lots ranging from 1 to 1.3 acres. The original
expiration date of the tentative map was October 26, 2020, and it was automatically extended to
April 26, 2022, by Assembly Bill (AB) 1561. A discretionary tentative map time extension
application (TM-E20-0005) was timely filed on October 7, 2020, requesting an additional three
(3) years (Exhibit G), which was approved by the Planning Commission on May 27, 2021
(Legistar File 21-0786). Finally, an additional 18-month extension was added by California AB
2729, granting this project an expiration date of October 1026, 2026.

This second discretionary tentative map time extension application (TM-E26-0001) was timely
filed on May 26, 2026, and requests an additional three (3) years, extending the expiration date
to October 26, 2029.

ANALYSIS

Section 120.74.030 of the El Dorado County Subdivision Ordinance regulates the discretionary
time extension of an approved tentative map. The ordinance limits the extension to a maximum
of six (6) one-year time extensions. The applicant previously requested a three-year extension
due to financial and economic concerns, particularly due to the COVID-19 pandemic and
meeting EID requirements regarding improvements to the water line. This second three-year
extension request is primarily due to a change in project ownership. If the extension is approved,
the map would be extended to October 1026, 2029. There have been no modifications to the
approved tentative map; therefore, the map remains consistent with the current 2017 tentative
map approval. All of the original Conditions of Approval and environmental mitigation measures
remain applicable.



                                                                         26-1601 A Page 2 of 4

TM-E26-0001/Southpointe Meadows
                                                                Planning Commission/October 22, 2026
                                                                                        Staff Report
                                                                                              Page 3


Based on the aforementioned information, staff recommends the Planning Commission grant the
requested three (3) one-year time extensions.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The Southpointe Meadows Tentative Subdivision Map is a residential project that was analyzed
in an Initial Study, resulting in the adoption of a Mitigated Negative Declaration for the approved
map.

The proposed time extension would allow the continued residential development of the
subdivision unit consistent with the tentative map environmental mitigation measures in the
adopted Mitigated Negative Declaration pursuant to CEQA. The time extension does not make
any changes to the original tentative map approval, does not involve new significant
environmental effects, and does not increase the severity of previously identified significant
effects. No new information that was not known and could not have been known at the time the
Mitigated Negative Declaration was certified has since become available. Therefore, this
tentative map time extension application is consistent with the approved Mitigated Negative
Declaration and is hereby exempt in accordance with Section 15162 of the CEQA Guidelines
(Subsequent EIRs and Negative Declarations). No further environmental analysis is needed, as
no changes have occurred in accordance with Sections 15162 and 15164 that would require any
supplemental or subsequent environmental documentation.

A $50.00 processing fee is required by the County Recorder to file the Notice of Exemption
(NOE) for the exemption determination made for this project by the County. This filing
establishes the 35-day statute of limitation during which the County’s determination can be
challenged.

            Date:                September 23, 2026                                             Agenda of: October 22, 2026

            To:                  Planning Commission

            From:                Lela Shelley, Associate Planner

            Subject:             ADM-A26-0001 Appeal of Administrative Permit, ADM26-0083 Black Rice Road Gate



            Recommendation

            Based on the analysis of Administrative Permit ADM26-0083, staff recommends the Planning
            Commission deny the Appeal (ADM-A26-0001) and uphold the approval of Administrative Permit
            ADM26-0083, based on the Findings and subject to the Compliance Standards as approved by the
            Planning and Building Department Director (Exhibit E).

            Alternative Action

            Grant the Appeal by Richard C. Nicolos (Appellant ADM-A26-0001), thereby denying Administrative
            Permit, ADM26-0083, and instruct staff to return with Findings for Denial.

            Background

            Administrative Permit ADM26-0083 approved a solar security gate at the cul-de-sac within Black Rice
            Road. The gate spans Black Rice Road (Exhibit B), a private road not maintained by the County, where
            two (2) or more residential lots are granted rights of access. Both the El Dorado County Fire Protection
            District (Fire District) and the El Dorado County Department of Transportation (DOT) reviewed ADM26-
            0083. The Fire District approved the gate with incorporation of conditions of approval (COA’s), and DOT
            takes no exception. Compliance Standards are incorporated within the Approval Letter (Exhibit E).

            The project is located at Assessor’s Parcel Number (APN) 051-461-069 (Exhibit A), a 5.71-acre property
            split zoned RE-5 (Residential Estate 5 acre minimum) and RM (Residential Multi-Unit) with a Planned
            Development (PD) overlay, located at 750 Black Rice Road in the Diamond Springs area, approximately
            1,585 feet east of the intersection with Highway 49, in Supervisorial District 3.

            At time of the Appeal, section 130.51.050.1 (Public Notice Requirements and Procedures –
            Administrative Projects) of the El Dorado County Zoning Ordinance did not include notification
            requirements for Administrative Permits for Gates; however, Planning staff determined that the proposed
            project is similar to the Administrative Permit requirements for Fences, Walls and Retaining Walls.
            Therefore, the 500-foot notification requirements for Administrative Permits for Fences, Walls and
            Retaining Walls were utilized for this project. Pursuant to Section 130.51.050.1 of the El Dorado County
                                                                                                      26-1602 B Page 1 of 4

ADM-A26-0001 Appeals of ADM26-0083 750 Black Rice Road Gate
                                                                    Planning Commission/October 22, 2026
                                                                          Staff Memo/September 23, 2026
                                                                                              Page 2 of 4

Zoning Ordinance, Administrative Permits are either required to have a 500-foot notification, 100-foot
notification, or no notification, based upon Administrative Permit type. The Notice of Decision letter
providing notification for the approval of ADM26-0083 was mailed to all property owners within a 500-
foot radius on August 17, 2026 (Exhibit F). On August 18, 2026 (Legistar File 26-1256), the Board of
Supervisors approved a Zoning Ordinance Update which went into effect September 18, 2026. This
update to table 130.51.050.1 Public Notice Requirements and Procedures – Administrative Projects,
identifies a 500-foot radius noticing requirement specifically for gates.

Section 130.30.090.C (Gates – Residential Subdivisions) of the El Dorado County Zoning Ordinance
allows gates across non-County maintained road(s) within a residential subdivision consisting of two (2)
or more lots with approval of an Administrative Permit when the following criteria are met: 1) The gate
will not impede public access to a public resource, such as a public park, or interfere with existing or
planned traffic circulation patterns; and 2) The project conforms to the standards of Subsection D (Design
Standards for Gated Developments).

ADM26-0083 proposed a solar security gate on 750 Black Rice Road that does not impede public access
to a public resource and conforms to applicable design standards.

Administrative Permits are a staff-level review with Director approval and appealable to the Planning
Commission. Administrative Permit ADM26-0083 was approved on August 27, 2026. Administrative
Permits are a ministerial project and are statutorily exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
(CEQA) per Section 15268 of the CEQA Guidelines. As a ministerial project, only adopted standards
may be applied.

Appeals Filed

On September 8, 2026, one (1) appeal was submitted in a timely manner in reference to the first Notice of
Decision. Appeal ADM-A26-0001 (Attachment 1), by Richard C. Nicolos was submitted appealing the
Director’s approval of Administrative Permit ADM26-0083 / Black Rice Road Gate. As stated in Appeal,
the appellant, Richard C. Nicolos, is objecting to the gate due to multiple concerns outlined below.

Staff Response

Below is a summary of staff’s response to the concerns stated in the submitted appeal.

Project Parcel and Description

Appeal ADM-A26-0001 states that the Administrative Permit application misidentifies the parcel that the
proposed gate burdens based on an inaccurate description of the project.

Staff Response: The project and application was applied for on APN 051-461-069 where the existing cul-
de-sac is located. The road easement for Black Rice Road is recorded as 50 feet wide non-exclusive Road
and Public Utility Easement (RPUE), 25’ of which is located on 051-461-069 and 25’ recorded on APN
051-461-022 (Appellant’s parcel) (Exhibit A and D). The proposed gate is within the recorded RPUE.




                                                                              26-1602 B Page 2 of 4

ADM-A26-0001 Appeals of ADM26-0083 750 Black Rice Road Gate
                                                                     Planning Commission/October 22, 2026
                                                                           Staff Memo/September 23, 2026
                                                                                               Page 3 of 4

Solid Waste Collection

Appeal ADM-A26-0001 states that the neighborhood’s solid waste collection point has been relocated to
the cul-de-sac where residents formerly conveyed their carts to a remote location near the intersection of
Black Rice Road and State Route 49.

Staff Response: The Black Rice Road Maintenance Agreement board is working with Waste Management
for a solution to the appropriate pick-up site for waste collection. This concern is not related nor relevant
to the gate installation, however truck turnaround and access has been available in the interim within the
existing cul-de-sac.

Ministerial vs. Discretionary Action

Appeal ADM-A26-0001 states that the Administrative Permit is not characterized as ministerial project
under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).

 Staff Response: Section 130.52.010 of the County of El Dorado Zoning Ordinance states that issuance of
an Administrative Permit shall be a ministerial project pursuant to CEQA. Review of the Administrative
Permit involves routing to applicable agencies for review to ensure application of applying fixed legal or
technical standards. These objective standards are within Section 130.30.090 of the County of El Dorado
Zoning Ordinance. This Administrative Permit does not require discretionary review.

Public Notice

Appeal ADM-A26-0001 states that the public notice radius was measured from the wrong parcel.

Staff Response: Exhibit G shows the required 500-foot radius from the property boundary of the project
parcel that the gate is proposed on for notification requirements. Seventy mailing labels were generated
based on this notification radius and the Notice of Decision letters were mailed. Three of the mailings
were returned unable to forward.

Circulation Findings

Appeal ADM-A26-0001 states that findings cannot be made that the gate will not interfere with existing
or planned traffic circulation patterns, and that vehicles that do not have access, will stop and turn around
directly in front of their parcel.

Staff Response: All property owners behind the gate will be given access to the solar gate with a code,
therefore the proposed project will not impede access to their properties. Additionally, visitors and
delivery vehicles for these property owners will need to be given the code by the applicable property
owner. The existing cul-de-sac can already be used as a turn around. The fire district approved the gate
with incorporation of conditions of approval and therefore should not have a significant effect on
emergency services.
